findings.defect: No pre-launch binding of the deck to the frozen case. cylinder_canary._attempt copies the manifest deck after checking only the manifest digest; cylinder_adapter.make_execution_adapters.launch verifies executable digest and reference provenance, then calls cylinder_runner.launch_case, whose _paths checks only existence/basename. build_case/validate_deck equality is enforced solely in extract_record, i.e. after the licensed solve has consumed an attempt. An approved manifest naming a non-frozen .inp executes arbitrary APDL under the B2 seat and the frozen four-case guarantee is post hoc only.
findings.correction: In the launch closure (and/or _attempt) read the copied deck bytes and require validate_deck(case['case_id'], raw) before _launch_case; add an adapter test that a manifest deck differing from build_case refuses launch with no _launch_case call.

findings.defect: cylinder_criteria.evaluate_canary returns dict(result, ...) when the fourth attempt is FAIL/INCOMPLETE, discarding the accumulated checks from attempts 1-3 (local 'checks' list) and never running _refinement. Via assessment_for_records (len==4 path) the receipt['checks'] for a final FAIL therefore omits the zero-control and coarse diagnostic checks the design says must be retained as diagnostics.
findings.correction: Return dict(result, checks=checks, ...) with the accumulated list (mirroring assessment_for_records' prefix branch); add a test asserting a final-attempt FAIL retains attempt 1-3 checks.

findings.defect: run_canary writes outcome.json outside the try/except. Any non-canonical value in the receipt (floats or non-JSON types in the adjudicator proof, a records entry, or an assess result from an external adapter) makes canonical_bytes raise in _save, so no durable receipt is written and the exception escapes with status already 'PASS' in memory. _adjudicate stores 'proof' without canonical validation.
findings.correction: In _adjudicate use proof = parse_json(canonical_bytes(proof)) before binding; in run_canary wrap the final _save so a canonicalisation failure writes a minimal INCOMPLETE receipt with the reason instead of losing the outcome.

findings.defect: cylinder_reference_provenance._git_blob spawns an unpinned 'git' resolved from PATH (14 invocations per verify, verify runs in prepare, launch and extract), which contradicts the adapter docstring 'Creating these callbacks never launches a process' and puts an unattested helper binary in the reference-agreement gate. It also requires working-tree bytes to equal raw blobs; on a Windows execution host with core.autocrlf=true the .py/.json/.txt FROZEN_FILES will differ (CRLF) and every B2 run will refuse before attempt 1.
findings.correction: Pin the git executable path (and optionally its digest) in the approval and pass it explicitly; document the helper-process fact; add/verify .gitattributes eol=lf for the frozen and evidence files or compare normalised bytes explicitly and record that choice.

findings.defect: _prepare_next reserves exactly 300 s (remaining() < 300) but a full attempt can take 300 s solve + up to 5 s settle + 5 s close + stream readback + extract-time provenance replay (dozens of git calls). A fourth attempt started at ~300 s remaining can legitimately overrun, and the later remaining() < 0 check then converts a fully consumed licensed solve into INCOMPLETE.
findings.correction: Reserve 300 s plus an explicit settlement/extract margin (e.g. 300 + 30 s) as a named constant, and assert the same margin in the time-budget test.
